acts.19.p1.b1.text: While Apollos was at Corinth, Paul passed through the interior and came to Ephesus. There he found some disciples

acts.19.p1.b2.text: “Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you became believers?”

acts.19.p1.b3.text: “No, … we have not even heard that there is a Holy Spirit.”

acts.19.p1.b4.text: “John’s baptism was a baptism of repentance. He told the people to believe in the One coming after him, that is, in Jesus.”

acts.19.p2.b5.text: On hearing this, they were baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus.

acts.19.p2.b6.text: And when Paul laid his hands on them, the Holy Spirit came upon them, and they spoke in tongues and prophesied.

acts.19.p2.b7.text: There were about twelve men in all.

acts.19.p3.b8.text: Then Paul went into the synagogue and spoke boldly there for three months, arguing persuasively about the kingdom of God.

acts.19.p3.b9.text: But when some of them stubbornly refused to believe and publicly maligned the Way, Paul took his disciples and left the synagogue

acts.19.p3.b10.text: to conduct daily discussions in the lecture hall of Tyrannus.

acts.19.p3.b11.text: This continued for two years, so that everyone who lived in the province of Asia, Jews and Greeks alike, heard the word of the Lord.

acts.19.p4.b12.text: God did extraordinary miracles through the hands of Paul,

acts.19.p4.b13.text: so that even handkerchiefs and aprons that had touched him were taken to the sick, and the diseases

acts.19.p5.b15.text: Now there were some itinerant Jewish exorcists who tried to invoke the name of the Lord Jesus over those with evil spirits. They would say,

acts.19.p5.b16.text: “I bind you by Jesus, whom Paul proclaims.”

acts.19.p5.b17.text: Seven sons of Sceva, a Jewish chief priest, were doing this.

acts.19.p6.b18.text: Eventually, one of the evil spirits answered them,

acts.19.p6.b19.text: “Jesus I know, and I know about Paul, but who are you?”

acts.19.p6.b20.text: Then the man with the evil spirit jumped on them and overpowered them all. The attack was so violent that they ran out of the house naked and wounded.

acts.19.p7.b21.text: This became known to all the Jews and Greeks living in Ephesus, and fear came over all of them.

acts.19.p7.b22.text: So the name of the Lord Jesus was held in high honor.

acts.19.p7.b23.text: Many who had believed now came forward, confessing and disclosing their deeds.

acts.19.p8.b24.text: And a number of those who had practiced magic arts brought their books and burned them in front of everyone.

acts.19.p8.b25.text: When the value of the books was calculated, the total came to fifty thousand drachmas.

acts.19.p8.b26.text: So the word of the Lord powerfully continued to spread and prevail.

acts.19.p9.b27.text: After these things had happened, Paul resolved in the Spirit to go to Jerusalem after he had passed through Macedonia and Achaia.

acts.19.p9.b28.text: “After I have been there, … I must see Rome as well.”

acts.19.p9.b29.text: He sent two of his helpers, Timothy and Erastus, to Macedonia,

acts.19.p9.b30.text: while he stayed for a time in the province of Asia.

acts.19.p10.b31.text: About that time there arose a great disturbance about the Way.

acts.19.p10.b32.text: It began with a silversmith named Demetrius who made silver shrines of Artemis, bringing much business to the craftsmen. Demetrius assembled the craftsmen, along with the workmen in related trades.

acts.19.p10.b33.text: “Men, … you know that this business is our source of prosperity. … Paul has persuaded a great number of people to turn away. He says that man-made gods are no gods at all.

acts.19.p10.b34.text: … her majesty deposed—she who is worshiped by all the province of Asia and the whole world.”

acts.19.p11.b36.text: dragging with them Gaius and Aristarchus, Paul’s traveling companions from Macedonia.

acts.19.p11.b37.text: Soon the whole city was in disarray.

acts.19.p11.b38.text: … They rushed together into the theatre,

acts.19.p12.b39.text: Paul wanted to go before the assembly, but the disciples would not allow him.

acts.19.p12.b40.text: Meanwhile the assembly was in turmoil. Some were shouting one thing and some another, and most of them did not even know why they were there.

acts.19.p12.b41.text: … he motioned for silence so he could make his defense to the people. But when they realized that he was a Jew,

acts.19.p12.b42.text: they all shouted in unison for about two hours: “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”

acts.19.p13.b43.text: Finally the city clerk quieted the crowd and declared,

acts.19.p13.b44.text: “Men of Ephesus, doesn’t everyone know that the city of Ephesus is guardian of the temple of the great Artemis and of her image, which fell from heaven?

acts.19.p13.b45.text: Since these things are undeniable, you ought to be calm and not do anything rash.

acts.19.p14.b46.text: So if Demetrius and his fellow craftsmen have a complaint against anyone, the courts are open and proconsuls are available. Let them bring charges against one another there.

acts.19.p14.b47.text: For we are in jeopardy of being charged with rioting for today’s events, and we have no justification to account for this commotion.”

acts.19.p14.b48.text: After he had said this, he dismissed the assembly.
